title: Digital Research and Judgment
text: Although digital tools have transformed academic research, they have not eliminated the need for critical judgment. Search systems can organize immense collections of information in seconds, allowing researchers to discover studies that would once have taken weeks to locate. However, speed does not guarantee reliability. A search engine may place a popular article beside a carefully reviewed academic paper, even though the two sources have different purposes and standards of evidence. Researchers must examine who produced each source, when it was published, and what evidence supports its claims. They must also consider what information may be missing. A study with a narrow sample, for example, may offer useful observations without representing an entire population. Digital tools are most valuable when they support thoughtful analysis rather than replace it.
